Mahender Singh And Ors vs Jaibir And Ors on 17 January, 2023
Fao-4697-2016 (O&M) 1
In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana

At Chandigarh
Fao-4697-2016 (O&M)
Pronounced on: 17.01.2023
Mahender Singh and others ... Appellants
Versus
Jaibir and others ...Respondents

Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Ritu Tagore Present: Mr. Amandeep Singh, Advocate for
Mr. Chanderhas Yadav, Advocate for the appellants.
Mr. Radhey Sham Sharma, Advocate for respondent No.3-Insurance Company.
ok 36 ok Ritu Tagore, J

1. This is an appeal filed by appellants-claimants against the award dated 12.08.2015 passed by Ld.
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal Gurugram, seeking enhancement in claim amount.

2. The deceased Jai Narayan, aged 79 years, had died in a motor vehicular accident on 10.05.2014
caused by respondent No.1 while driving the offending vehicle, a motorcycle, bearing registration
No.HR-01-V-6474, rashly and negligently.
3.  The claimants filed the petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Upon notice,
the respondent No.1, driver and respondent No.2, owner put up an appearance and resisted the petition by pleading their false implication in the accident by denying the same.
The insurer (respondent No.3) did not put up an appearance before the Ld. Tribunal and was proceeded against ex-parte.
On assessment of evidence, the Ld. Tribunal granted MANPREET SINGH - i MANPREET SINGH Rg_46,000/- as compensation.

Ld. counsel for the claimants restricts the prayer for reassessment of compensation based on the directions given by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the judgments titled 'National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others' (2017) 16 SCC 680, N. Jayasree and Ors. vs.
Cholamandlam_ MS General Ins. Co. Ltd.'2021 ACJ 2685 and 'Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others' (2018) 18 SCC 130 stating that the Ld. Tribunal has failed to account for future prospects on the assessed income of the deceased and compensation under the conventional heads.

However, raises no dispute of the liability of the Insurance Company to pay the award amount.
6. In Pranay Sethi (supra), it is observed that 'there should be an addition of 15% if the deceased is between the age 50 to 60 years and there should be no addition, thereafter.
Similarly, in case of self-employed or person on a fixed salary, the addition should be 10% between the age 50 to 60 years.'
Since the deceased was 79 years at the time of his accidental death, no addition is required to be made towards future prospects.

In the afore cited celebrated judgment, the Hon'ble Apex Court further observed that 'the vanpreetsincy Claims Tribunals shall be guided by Step 2 that finds place in Para 19 read Taitest o the acu racy and authenticity of this order/judgment FAO-4697-2016 (O&M) 3 with Para 42 of the judgment Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, 2009 (3) R.C.R. (Civil) 77 while applying the multiplier based on the age of the deceased'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the age of the deceased at 79 years, no multiplier is required to be applied.

Based on the number of the claimants, deduction of 1/3" towards personal expenses as adopted by the Ld.
Tribunal is justified.
7. I have considered the submissions as raised.
The question falls for determination before this Court is whether the income of the deceased is required to be enhanced or not?

Except for the oral account, the claimants led no cogent evidence to show that the deceased was actively pursuing the agricultural activities and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month from agricultural work.
No lease deed (Pattanama) or revenue record has been placed on record to substantiate the version that the deceased was a farmer by occupation.
The claimants have examined no other person to establish on record that the deceased was doing the claimed work and had the claimed earnings.

Keeping in view the evidence led by the claimants and the advance age of the deceased, this Court considers that the Ld. Tribunal has rightly taken the income and the services of the deceased towards the family at Rs.2,000/-.
In the facts, no addition in the income of the deceased is called for.
The grant of Rs.15,996/- towards loss of income has been rightly determined by the Ld. Tribunal.

Similarly,
allowing Rs.4,747/- as expenses on the treatment is in tune with the medical bills Exh.P-10 to P-14.
8.
It is a settled proposition in law that an appeal is a continuation of original proceedings.
Thus, the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (supra) would apply in the present case as the order passed by the Ld. Tribunal is under challenge in the present appeal.

In given facts and VANPREET sincy Cifcumstances, the grant of compensation under the conventional heads needs Taitest o the acu racy and authenticity of this order/judgment FAO-4697-2016 (O&M) 4 to be revised.

9. Keeping in view the ratio of the above cited judgments and Sidram vs. The Divisional Manager,
United India Insurance Co. Ltd. and another' 2023 (1) R.C.R. (Civil) 44, of the Hon'ble Apex Court,
the compensation is recalculated as under:-

7. Loss of consortium (parental) i.e. Rs.1,32,000/- Rs. 44,000/- x 3 8.

The Insurance company-respondent No.3, is directed to pay the claimants-appellants the enhanced amount of compensation Rs.1,64,743/- (One Lakh Sixty Four Thousand Seven Hundred and Forty Three only) awarded, hereinabove, as against the amount awarded by the Ld. Tribunal, at the rate of interest as granted by the Ld. Tribunal from filing of the claim petition till its realization,
within two months from receipt of certified copy of this judgment, with the Ld. Tribunal.
Remaining conditions of disbursal of the 20280117 15:27 amount as given by the Ld. Tribunal shall remain unaltered.

Needless to | attest to the accuracy'al authenticity of this order/judgment MANPREET SINGH 2023.01.17 15:27 FAO-4697-2016 (O&M) 5 mention that the amount, if any, already deposited by the insurance company shall be adjusted.
11. The appeal stands allowed in the aforesaid terms.
No order as to costs.
12. Pending miscellaneous application, if any, stand disposed of.
